newsitem.title: USA: Heinz backs FY '97 EPS estimates.
newsitem.headline: Heinz backs FY '97 EPS estimates.

text.p: H.J. Heinz Co is on track to meet Wall Street's consensus earnings estimate of $1.92 per share in the fiscal year 1997, Heinz Chairman Anthony O'Reilly said Tuesday.
O'Reilly made his comments at a news conference following the company's annual shareholders' meeting.
Heinz earned $1.75 per share in fiscal year 1996.
During the meeting, O'Reilly told shareholders the company is reviewing its assets, a process that could result in some divestitures.
"We are undertaking a review of all our assets with a view to restructuring our portfolio and ensuring the maximum capital profits for our shareholders," he said.
He said any profits realized from asset sales would be used to reduce debt, write off underperforming assets, and pay for any resulting organizational changes.

At the conference, O'Reilly declined to give any details about divestitures but suggested that they would not affect what the company considers its six core businesses: food service, infant foods, ketchup and condiments, pet food, tuna, and weight control.

He said the company is focused on positioning itself as a world leader in those lines of businesses. Moreover, he said any asset sale profits would not be counted toward the company's achieving its previously stated goal of double-digit earnings growth over the next few years.
